name: RichTextArea

knownIssues.summary: In Firefox and Safari the caret can drift out of the `/` query box at its edge: the box is an inline editable span, and there's no caret-correction guard yet (checked only in Chrome).
Backspace doesn't remove a tag as one unit in every position: the tag is atomic to the caret, but the surrounding deletion cases aren't fully handled.

Pasted rich HTML isn't sanitized into the value's node model; multi-line serialization handles `
` but not every paste shape.

purpose: Let a user write multi-line text that mixes plain prose with inline links to real records - typing `/` opens a grouped entity picker and each choice is inserted as a navigational tag.
intent: Text Area's `type=rich-inline` mode, built as its own component because the contenteditable path and its props are disjoint from the plain <textarea>. It reuses Text Area's frame tokens exactly, so the two read as one field; the difference is entirely behavioral. Composes the Menu organism as the picker and the Tag atom as the inserted tag, rather than inventing either.

figmaSource.note: Shares Text Area's component set - `type=rich-inline` is one axis value there, visually identical to `default`. The picker's own anatomy was built from the `type-cursor` figma-part added to text-field on 2026-08-28 (open-search / type-to-search variants) fed into a dropdown-menu variant with a defined open menu. Because the mode is behavior, not appearance, most of this component has no static Figma counterpart to verify against.
figmaSource.structure: The editor frame is Text Area's frame, token-for-token. The `/` mini-input reuses Text Field's look (background, input border, radius) at a small size, per the Figma type-cursor part. The picker is the menu organism with search hidden - the query is typed inline in the editor, not in the panel - with one section per entity type and a 16px IconTile heading.
apiAdaptationNotes: Built as a separate `RichTextArea` component rather than a `type` prop on TextArea. The two share a frame but nothing else: one is a native <textarea> with a string value, the other is a contenteditable surface with a structured node array, `onSearch`, and an entity config. A single component would have had two disjoint prop sets and two disjoint values.

The value is a flat node array (`RichTextValue`) - runs of text interleaved with entity nodes - not HTML or Markdown. It is what you persist; serialize it however your store needs. Storing HTML would leak the editor's DOM shape into consumers' data.

Hydrates from `value` once, then runs uncontrolled - the DOM is the source of truth while editing, with `onChange` reporting each serialized change. A contenteditable surface cannot be re-rendered from props on every keystroke without destroying the caret.

The `/` query lives in an inline editable span inside the editor (the Figma `type-cursor` look), so the picker panel has no search field of its own - `showSearch={false}`. This matches Figma and mirrors how Select types in the trigger while the panel only lists options.

Focus stays in the editor while the picker is open; the keyboard-active row is marked with a class rather than by moving focus, so typing continues to land in the `/` span. The editor's aria-activedescendant points assistive technology at that row (the picker gives each row the id `<pickerId>-option-<index>`), and aria-controls names the picker's Menu while it is open.

Figma's text-area `context` axis (default/inline) is the `context` prop, as on Text Area. It replaces the earlier `appearance` prop (default/subtle/inline), which is deprecated but still accepted: subtle and inline map to context=inline, default to context=default; an explicit context wins.

Each tag is a non-editable host span with a `NavTag` portaled into it. contenteditable would otherwise let the caret walk into the tag's internals; a host span keeps each tag atomic to the caret while still being a real React subtree.
`NavTag` is a preset over the Tag atom, not a new component - Tag already does tone (color), `elemBefore` (icon), and `href` (navigation). An entityType only needs to resolve to a tone plus an icon.
Non-empty queries are debounced 150ms; an empty query resolves immediately from `recents` (or `onSearch('')`) so opening the picker feels instant.
`scrollIntoView` on the active row is called optionally - jsdom does not implement it, and an unguarded call throws inside any consumer's test.

useCases: a note or comment that mentions people, matters, or documents by name
text where each mention should link to the record it names

anatomy.description: The frame and the editable surface in one: Text Area's frame tokens around the text and the inline tags. It sits in a div.wrapper, the same size, which positions the picker and takes className.
One per linked entity: a non-editable host span with a NavTag (a Tag atom, an <a> when href is set) portaled into it, so the caret treats the tag as one unit.
Only while a / command is active: the typed /query in a small bordered box inside the text, showing searchPlaceholder until a query is typed.
Only while a / command is active: the floating list of matching entities, grouped by type - the Menu organism with its search hidden, positioned under the query.

value.description: The node array: `{ type: 'text', text }` runs interleaved with `{ type: 'entity', entity }` nodes. Read on mount to hydrate the editor; the DOM leads from then on.

onChange.description: Called with the re-serialized node array after every edit, including tag insertion and deletion.

onSearch.description: `(query: string) => EntitySection[] | Promise<EntitySection[]>`. Resolves the `/query` into grouped results. Called with '' when the picker opens unless `recents` is supplied.

recents.description: Shown when the picker opens with an empty query, instead of calling `onSearch('')`.

entityConfig.description: Maps each entityType to a tag `tone` and a default `icon`, used for both the inserted tag and the section heading tile. Merges over the built-in defaults.

size.description: Text Area's frame sizing - padding, radius, font. sm keeps md's corners, inline padding, and text, with Text Area's tighter block padding (--spacing-075).

context.description: Where it's shown, as on Text Area and Figma's text-area. default = the bordered field. inline = chromeless at rest; the hover background and a bottom line in color-border-input on hover (not while invalid or focused), and a 2px bottom line on focus or error.

appearance.description: Deprecated - use context. subtle and inline map to context='inline', default to 'default'. Still accepted; an explicit context wins.

resize.description: Which edges the user can drag.

invalid.description: Sets aria-invalid and paints the error border, which stays while the editor has focus.

disabled.description: Turns off contenteditable, removes the editor from the tab order, sets aria-disabled, and suppresses the slash command.

required.description: Sets aria-required on the editor (a div has no native required). Field passes it when its own required is set.

placeholder.description: Shown while the editor is empty. Rendered from `data-placeholder` as an absolutely-positioned overlay, so it never sits in the text flow or displaces the caret.

searchPlaceholder.description: Placeholder inside the `/` mini-input before a query is typed.

emptyMessage.description: Shown in the picker when a search returns nothing.

rows.description: Starting height in line-height units, applied as the `--rta-rows` custom property to the editor's min-height. The editor grows past it as content is added.

id.description: Applied to the editor element. A <label htmlFor> cannot name it - the editor is a div, not a labelable element - so pair a visible label through aria-labelledby (Field does this with its label's id).

aria-label.description: Accessible name for the editor. Required unless aria-labelledby is used.

aria-labelledby.description: Accessible name by reference. Field passes its label's id.

aria-describedby.description: Ids of elements that describe the editor, such as Field's message.

aria-invalid.description: true or 'true' marks the editor invalid, as invalid does (aria-invalid plus the error border). Field passes it for an error.

default.purpose: The standard bordered box - correct for nearly every case.

inline.purpose: Chromeless at rest; the hover background and a bottom line on hover, a 2px bottom line on focus or error. For a low-chrome inline composer or a field inside a row.

accessibility.label: No built-in label - pass aria-label, or aria-labelledby pointing at a visible label. A <label htmlFor> wired to `id` does not name it, because the editor is a div. Field names it anyway by passing its label's id as aria-labelledby, and its aria-describedby, aria-invalid, and required (as aria-required) land on the editor too.
accessibility.invalid: aria-invalid reflects the invalid prop, or an aria-invalid of true/'true' passed in.
accessibility.required: required sets aria-required on the editor.
accessibility.description: aria-describedby is set on the editor as given (Field passes its message's id).
accessibility.disabled: contenteditable is turned off, tabIndex is -1, and aria-disabled is set; the slash command does not fire.
accessibility.tags: Each tag renders a Tag with tabIndex -1 so the caret walk is not interrupted by tab stops; a tag with `href` is a real <a> and is reachable from the rendered content.
accessibility.picker: Focus deliberately stays in the editor so typing continues to reach the `/` query. While the picker is open, aria-controls names its Menu and aria-activedescendant points at the highlighted row (each row's id is `<pickerId>-option-<index>`), so the active entity is announced; both are removed when it closes. Tab closes the picker and lets focus move on.

behaviorRules: Render a contenteditable div (role=textbox, aria-multiline="true", aria-haspopup="menu") with Text Area's frame, inside a wrapper div that positions the picker and takes className.
Default size=md, context=default, resize=vertical, rows=3, searchPlaceholder="Type to search", emptyMessage="No matches".
The deprecated appearance prop maps to context: subtle and inline map to inline, default to default. An explicit context wins.

Hydrate the editor from value once, on mount; after that the DOM leads, onChange reports the whole re-serialized node array after every edit (including adding or removing a tag), and a value passed later is ignored.
`/` starts a command only at the start of the editor or after whitespace; anywhere else it is typed as a slash.

While a command is active, the query is typed into an inline span.slashInput (showing searchPlaceholder until a query is typed) and the picker opens under it, grouped into one Menu section per EntitySection.
An empty query resolves immediately from recents when given, otherwise from onSearch(''); non-empty queries are debounced 150ms, and a response to an older query never replaces a newer one.
With the picker open, ArrowDown/ArrowUp move the active row, clamped at both ends; Enter inserts the active row as a tag followed by a space, replacing the /query span.
Escape, a space, the caret leaving the query span, or a pointer press outside the field closes the picker and keeps what was typed as plain text. Tab closes it the same way and lets focus move on.

Focus stays in the editor while the picker is open; aria-controls names the picker's Menu and aria-activedescendant points at the active row (id `<pickerId>-option-<index>`), and both are removed when it closes.

Each tag is a non-editable host span with a NavTag (a Tag with tabIndex -1, an <a> when the entity has href), so the caret treats it as one unit. Its tone and icon come from entityConfig, merged over the built-in tones (account and person blue, matter teal, roadmap purple, document default).
Deleting a tag leaves the space after it, which is ordinary text.
invalid, or an aria-invalid of true/'true', sets aria-invalid and the error border, which stays while the editor has focus.

disabled turns off contenteditable, sets tabIndex -1 and aria-disabled, and suppresses the slash command. A disabled <fieldset> around the editor (outside its first legend) does the same, and the component follows changes to its disabled attribute.
required sets aria-required; id, aria-label, aria-labelledby, and aria-describedby go on the editor. A <label htmlFor> cannot name it; Field names it with aria-labelledby.
The editor starts rows lines tall (the --rta-rows custom property) and grows with its content without limit; dragging the resize grip sets a fixed height, after which it scrolls.
placeholder shows while the editor is empty, as an overlay from data-placeholder, never in the text flow.

tokens.frame: All of Text Area's frame tokens, unchanged - surface, border, radius, padding, typography per size.
tokens.tagHost: Layout only - the Tag atom carries its own tone tokens.
tokens.picker: The Menu organism's own panel tokens; the panel caps at 280px and scrolls.
tokens.note: No new tokens. Frame reuse is what makes the rich mode read as the same field as Text Area.

do: Give the editor an accessible name (aria-label, aria-labelledby, or wrap it in Field, which names it with aria-labelledby).
Return grouped sections from `onSearch`, one per entity type, so the picker reads as categories rather than a flat list.
Give each entityType a distinct tone in `entityConfig` so color encodes type consistently in both the picker row and the inserted tag.
Supply `recents` so opening the picker with an empty query is instant and useful.
Persist the node array as-is, or map it to your own shape - it is a stable, serializable structure.
dont: Don't use it for plain multi-line text - use TextArea, which is a real <textarea> with native behavior.
Don't treat the value as HTML or Markdown - it is a flat node array by design.
Don't re-render it from `value` on every keystroke expecting the editor to follow; it hydrates once and then leads.
acceptanceCriteria: Renders a multiline textbox (role=textbox, aria-multiline) with aria-haspopup="menu".
Defaults to size=md and resize=vertical; applies each size, context, and resize value; the deprecated appearance maps subtle and inline to context=inline.
Takes the wiring Field passes: named by aria-labelledby, described by aria-describedby, aria-required from required, aria-invalid from aria-invalid.
invalid sets aria-invalid and data-invalid on the editor.
placeholder is exposed as data-placeholder with data-empty while empty; rows sets --rta-rows.
disabled is not editable, not focusable, aria-disabled, and never opens the picker; a disabled fieldset around it does the same and its changes are followed, except inside the fieldset's legend.
Hydrates text and entity nodes from value, each entity as a navigational tag, and a newline in a text node as a line break.
`/` opens the picker and wraps the query in the slash input only at the start or after whitespace; ordinary typing leaves the picker closed and never calls onSearch.
An empty query shows recents instead of searching; a typed query searches.

Enter inserts the active entity and reports the new value; ArrowUp/ArrowDown move the active row and stop at the ends; Escape closes the picker and leaves the query as plain text; Tab closes it and removes aria-controls.
aria-activedescendant points at the highlighted row while the picker is open, and is absent while it is closed.
onChange reports text and entities in document order, and drops an entity when its tag is removed.
Storybook includes Playground, Prefilled, States, and Variants.

Tests cover rendering, Field wiring, disabled (including fieldsets), hydration, the slash lifecycle, picker keyboard and aria-activedescendant, and serialization. Real caret behavior is verified live in Storybook (Chrome), since jsdom cannot simulate contenteditable typing.
behaviorNotes: Inside a disabled <fieldset> (outside its first legend), the editor is disabled as with disabled: not editable, out of the tab order, aria-disabled. A div isn't disabled by a fieldset natively, so the component checks the fieldsets around it and watches their disabled attribute.
`/` only starts a command at the beginning of the editor or after whitespace - mid-word slashes stay literal characters.
The query types inline into a small bordered span; Escape (or a caret leaving the span) unwraps it back to plain text, keeping what was typed.
Enter inserts the active row as a tag, replacing the `/query` span and adding a trailing space.
That trailing space is ordinary text - deleting a tag afterwards leaves the space behind.
ArrowUp/ArrowDown move the active row and are clamped at both ends.
A pointer press outside the field closes the picker.
Tab with the picker open closes it, keeping the typed text, and lets focus move on.
An empty query resolves from `recents` when provided; non-empty queries are debounced 150ms, and out-of-order responses are discarded by sequence number.
knownLimitations: No maxRows: the editor grows with its content from the `rows` minimum without limit, and dragging the resize grip sets a fixed height, after which it scrolls.

Tests cover rendering, hydration, the slash lifecycle, picker keyboard, and serialization. They cannot cover real caret behavior - jsdom does not simulate contenteditable typing - so caret correctness is verified live in Storybook, not in CI.
futureEnhancements: A caret-correction guard for Firefox/Safari at the inline span boundary.
Harden backspace-deletes-a-tag and paste handling, including sanitizing pasted HTML into the node model.
Async loading affordance in the picker beyond the Menu's own loading row.
Mention-style triggers beyond `/` (for example `@`), driven by the same picker.
